claim: HSPCs were isolated from bone marrow by flushing femurs, tibia, and iliac crests.
source: A single-cell suspension was obtained by flushing femurs, tibia, and iliac crests.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental procedure for obtaining cells, and Figure 1 illustrates this process.

claim: Cells were stained with fluorescently labeled antibodies for phenotypic identification before CellTrace staining.
source: Cells were stained with fluorescently labeled antibodies for phenotypic identification. After this first antibody staining, the cell suspension was then split into four equal parts, each of which was stained with a distinct 5-(and 6)-carboxyfluorescein diacetate succinimidyl ester (CFSE) and CellTrace Violet (CTV) combination.
evidence: The experimental procedure is described in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Four distinctly CTV/CFSE-colored cells were sorted per well.
source: From each of these CTV/CFSE preparations, a single cell was index sorted into 90 wells of a 96-well plate, resulting in four distinctly CTV/CFSE-colored cells per well.
evidence: The sorting strategy is described in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Cells were cultured for 24 or 48 hours.
source: After 24 or 48 hr of culture, cells were stained with fluorescently labeled antibodies for phenotypic identification and analyzed on a flow cytometer.
evidence: The culture duration is stated in the methods description and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Three HSPC populations were defined: c-Kit+Sca-1+CD150+Flt3- (SLAM-HSC), c-Kit+Sca-1+CD150-Flt3- (ST-HSC), and c-Kit+Sca-1+CD150-Flt3+ (MPP).
source: To this end, we isolated bone marrow (BM) cells, labeled them with four distinguishable combinations of 5-(and 6)-carboxyfluorescein diacetate succinimidyl ester (CFSE) and CellTrace Violet (CTV), and used fluorescent antibody staining of cell surface markers to determine three HSPC populations, c-Kit+Sca-1+CD150+Flt3- (SLAM-HSC), c-Kit+Sca-1+CD150-Flt3- (ST-HSC), and c-Kit+Sca-1+CD150-Flt3+ (MPP) (Figure 1).
evidence: The cell populations are explicitly defined based on surface marker expression.

claim: From 600 seeded SLAM-HSCs, 358 families (71%) were recovered constituting 648 cells.
source: From the 600 seeded SLAM-HSCs, we recovered 358 families (71%) constituting 648 cells, while 343 ST-HSC families (69%) were recovered with 592 cells, and 246 MPP families (49%) with 362 cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The recovery rates are quantified from experimental data.

claim: 343 ST-HSC families (69%) were recovered with 592 cells.
source: From the 600 seeded SLAM-HSCs, we recovered 358 families (71%) constituting 648 cells, while 343 ST-HSC families (69%) were recovered with 592 cells, and 246 MPP families (49%) with 362 cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The recovery rates are quantified from experimental data.

claim: 246 MPP families (49%) were recovered with 362 cells.
source: From the 600 seeded SLAM-HSCs, we recovered 358 families (71%) constituting 648 cells, while 343 ST-HSC families (69%) were recovered with 592 cells, and 246 MPP families (49%) with 362 cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The recovery rates are quantified from experimental data.

claim: 27 families (2.8% of recovered families) had cell numbers that could not have originated from a single ancestor and were excluded from analysis.
source: Over all conditions, 27 families (2.8% of recovered families) had cell numbers that could not have originated from a single ancestor, and so were excluded from analysis, illustrating the fidelity of the single-cell sorting.
evidence: The exclusion criteria and number of excluded families are stated based on experimental observations.

claim: A diversity of myeloid cell types ranging from the initial ancestor to c-Kit- differentiated cells was obtained in both culture conditions and for each ancestor type.
source: In both culture conditions and for each ancestor type, we obtained a diversity of myeloid cell types ranging from the initial ancestor to c-Kit- differentiated cells, including c-Kit+Sca-1-CD16/32+ (GMP), c-Kit+Sca-1-CD150-CD16/32- (CMP/MEP), c-Kit-CD16/32+ (late myeloid progenitor, late MP), and c-Kit-CD16/32 cell types (Figure 2A).
evidence: The cell types observed are described based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: c-Kit+Sca-1-CD150+CD16/32- (PreMegE) cells were detected, previously described as megakaryocyte and erythroid progenitors (Pronk et al., 2007).
source: We also detected c-Kit+Sca-1-CD16/32CD150+ (PreMegE) cells, previously described as megakaryocyte and erythroid progenitors (Pronk et al., 2007).
evidence: The cell type is identified in the data and its identity is supported by a citation.

claim: No offspring of SLAM-HSCs, and those of very few ST-HSCs, differentiated into Flt3 expressing MPPs in the culture conditions used.
source: Although all hematopoietic cells have been reported to go through a Flt3 expressing stage (Boyer et al., 2011), we found that no offspring of SLAM-HSCs, and those of very few ST-HSCs, differentiated into Flt3 expressing MPPs in our culture conditions (Figure 2D).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Some ST-HSC and MPP acquired CD150 expression after culture, making them resemble SLAM-HSCs.
source: Some ST-HSC and MPP acquired CD150 expression after culture, making them resemble SLAM-HSCs, but this was not further investigated.
evidence: The observation is stated based on experimental data.

claim: CD150 expression cannot be due to residual fluorescence from antibodies used for cell sorting as no fluorescence was measured for any of the markers in cells kept for 24 hr in culture after sorting without further antibodies staining.
source: This CD150 expression cannot be due to residual fluorescence from antibodies used for cell sorting as no fluorescence was measured for any of the markers in cells kept for 24 hr in culture after sorting without further antibodies staining (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The addition of IL-3 and IL-6 had no impact on the pattern of cell types produced by SLAM-HSCs.
source: The addition of IL-3 and IL-6 had no impact on the pattern of cell types produced by SLAM-HSCs (Figure 2D).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The addition of IL-3 and IL-6 changed the pattern of cell types produced by ST-HSCs and MPPs in a statistically significant way.
source: It did, however, change the pattern of cell types produced by ST-HSCs and MPPs in a statistically significant way as determined by a permutation test (Materials and methods), with an increased number of early progenitors as opposed to more differentiated progenitors as previously shown (Lui et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Substantial heterogeneity in division history was observed from families that did not proliferate to those with cells that had undergone six divisions.
source: At the level of individual families, we observed substantial heterogeneity in division history (Figure 2E) from families that did not proliferate to those with cells that had undergone six divisions.
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: After 24 hr most cells either remained undivided or had divided once, with a few cells having undergone two or more divisions.
source: Consistent with earlier observations (Roch et al., 2017), after 24 hr most cells either remained undivided or had divided once, with a few cells having undergone two or more divisions (Figure 2A).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: At 48 hr, over 90% of the cells had undergone at least one division.
source: At 48 hr, over 90% of the cells had undergone at least one division.
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data.

claim: For all three sorted ancestor cell types, addition of IL-3 and IL-6 led to a statistically significant increase in proliferation.
source: For all three sorted ancestor cell types, we found that addition of IL-3 and IL-6 led to a statistically significant increase in proliferation (Figure 2E), as previously described (Domen and Weissman, 2000; Bordeaux-Rego et al., 2010).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2E and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: In the culture without IL-3 and IL-6, the proportion of undivided ancestors that differentiated were 36.5% from SLAM-HSCs, 61.1% from ST-HSCs, and 35.6% from MPPs.
source: Exploring the relationship between division and differentiation, in the culture without IL-3 and IL-6, the proportion of undivided ancestors that differentiated were 36.5% from SLAM-HSCs, 61.1% from ST-HSCs, and 35.6% from MPPs (Figure 2F), which was in agreement with previous reports (Roch et al., 2015; Grinenko et al., 2018).
evidence: The proportions are calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 2F and are consistent with previous literature.

claim: SLAM-HSCs preferentially differentiated without dividing into PreMegEs.
source: SLAM-HSCs preferentially differentiated without dividing into PreMegEs, as reported previously (Grinenko et al., 2018).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Sca-1high SLAM-HSCs were more likely not to differentiate.
source: On comparing the surface marker expression of differentiated and not-differentiated non-divided cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), Sca-1high SLAM-HSCs were more likely not to differentiate, in agreement with a previous report (Schulte et al., 2015).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: The addition of IL-3 and IL-6 only significantly impacted the differentiation pattern of the progeny of MPPs.
source: The addition of IL-3 and IL-6 only significantly impacted the differentiation pattern of the progeny of MPPs.
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data.

claim: 70.7% of the cells had a symmetric fate after their first division.
source: Pooling data over ancestor types, 70.7% of the cells had a symmetric fate after their first division, with the fate of MPPs being mostly symmetric undifferentiated (51.4%), and of ST-HSC being mostly symmetric differentiated (59.5%).
evidence: The proportions are calculated from experimental data.

claim: The fate of MPPs after first division was mostly symmetric undifferentiated (51.4%).
source: Pooling data over ancestor types, 70.7% of the cells had a symmetric fate after their first division, with the fate of MPPs being mostly symmetric undifferentiated (51.4%), and of ST-HSC being mostly symmetric differentiated (59.5%).
evidence: The proportion is calculated from experimental data.

claim: The fate of ST-HSC after first division was mostly symmetric differentiated (59.5%).
source: Pooling data over ancestor types, 70.7% of the cells had a symmetric fate after their first division, with the fate of MPPs being mostly symmetric undifferentiated (51.4%), and of ST-HSC being mostly symmetric differentiated (59.5%).
evidence: The proportion is calculated from experimental data.

claim: SLAM-HSCs self-renewed with symmetric undifferentiated fates (32.1%) and with asymmetric undifferentiated fates (10.7%).
source: SLAM-HSCs self-renewed with symmetric undifferentiated fates (32.1%), but also with asymmetric undifferentiated fates (10.7%).
evidence: The proportions are calculated from experimental data.

claim: Asymmetric fates occurred for 28.6% of SLAM-HSCs, 28.6% of ST-HSCs, and 31.4% of MPPs.
source: Asymmetric fates occurred for 28.6% of SLAM-HSCs, 28.6% of ST-HSCs, and 31.4% of MPPs, consistent with previous reports (Suda et al., 1984).
evidence: The proportions are calculated from experimental data and are consistent with previous literature.

claim: No statistical difference was found between ancestors cultured with or without IL-3 and IL-6 in terms of symmetric versus asymmetric fates after first division.
source: No statistical difference was found between ancestors cultured with or without IL-3 and IL-6.
evidence: The observation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: 81% of the 223 families that divided more than once had all of their cells in the same generation (range = 0).
source: We found that families are highly concordant, with 81% of the 223 families that divided more than once having all of their cells in the same generation (range = 0, Figure 2H), and only four of those families (1.8%) containing cells that were more than one generation apart (range >1, Figure 2H).
evidence: The proportion is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Only four families (1.8%) contained cells that were more than one generation apart (range >1).
source: We found that families are highly concordant, with 81% of the 223 families that divided more than once having all of their cells in the same generation (range = 0, Figure 2H), and only four of those families (1.8%) containing cells that were more than one generation apart (range >1, Figure 2H).
evidence: The proportion is calculated from experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: High correlation coefficients (70–90%) resulted in the best fit to the measured familial ranges for SLAM-HSC, ST-HSC, and MPP families cultured with IL-3 and IL-6.
source: High correlation coefficients (70–90%) (Figure 2H) resulted in the best fit to the measured familial ranges, with the exception of MPPs cultured in medium without IL-3 and IL-6 for which no reliable estimate could be made.
evidence: The correlation coefficients are derived from mathematical modeling of experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Division progression is highly concordant within SLAM-HSC, ST-HSC, and MPP families, while being heterogeneous between them.
source: Thus, this analysis establishes that division progression is highly concordant within SLAM-HSC, ST-HSC, and MPP families, while being heterogeneous between them.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data and mathematical modeling.

claim: Differentiation progressed in tandem with division.
source: Although differentiation without division was observed, in general differentiation progressed in tandem with division (Figure 3A), as published previously (Upadhaya et al., 2018).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3A and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: A smooth transition was observed from SLAM-HSCs at the bottom of the UMAP, with further differentiated cells towards the top, indicating a gradual transition from one cell type to another.
source: When we mapped cell types determined by traditional gating onto the UMAP (Figure 3C), a smooth transition was observed from SLAM-HSCs at the bottom, with further differentiated cells towards the top, indicating a gradual transition from one cell type to another.
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: GMPs and MPs appear on the top left of the UMAP, and CMP/MEP and PreMegE on the top right.
source: GMPs and c-Kit-Sca-1-CD16/32+ (myeloid progenitors [MPs]) appear on the top left, and CMP/MEP and PreMegE on the top right.
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: More numerous GMPs, MPs, and CMP/MEPs were seen at the top of the UMAP at 48 hr than 24 hr, suggesting that it takes between 24 and 48 hr to fully differentiate into Sca1- progenitors.
source: More numerous GMPs, MPs, and CMP/MEPs were seen at the top of the UMAP at 48 hr than 24 hr, suggesting that it takes between 24 and 48 hr to fully differentiate into Sca1- progenitors.
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 3C, and the suggestion is an inference from the data.

claim: All three ancestral cell types remain present at 48 hr, demonstrating that HSCs can remain in an undifferentiated state for the duration of the experiment, even if their offspring experience three rounds of division.
source: In addition, all three ancestral cell types remain present at 48 hr, demonstrating, in particular, that HSCs can remain in an undifferentiated state for the duration of the experiment, even if their offspring experience three rounds of division.
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: SLAM-HSCs appeared to be primed towards the production of CMP/MEPs and PreMegEs while still generating some ST-HSCs.
source: On plotting the generation numbers of offspring from each ancestor cell type on the UMAP (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), SLAM-HSCs appeared to be primed towards the production of CMP/MEPs and PreMegEs while still generating some ST-HSCs, whereas MPPs were more primed towards GMPs, and ST-HSCs showed a more even distribution between the two lineages.
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: MPPs were more primed towards GMPs.
source: On plotting the generation numbers of offspring from each ancestor cell type on the UMAP (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), SLAM-HSCs appeared to be primed towards the production of CMP/MEPs and PreMegEs while still generating some ST-HSCs, whereas MPPs were more primed towards GMPs, and ST-HSCs showed a more even distribution between the two lineages.
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ST-HSCs showed a more even distribution between the two lineages (CMP/MEP/PreMegE and GMP).
source: On plotting the generation numbers of offspring from each ancestor cell type on the UMAP (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), SLAM-HSCs appeared to be primed towards the production of CMP/MEPs and PreMegEs while still generating some ST-HSCs, whereas MPPs were more primed towards GMPs, and ST-HSCs showed a more even distribution between the two lineages.
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: PreMegEs were observed to be generated without division, as well as in 1–3 divisions from SLAM-HSCs.
source: PreMegEs were observed to be generated without division, as well as in 1–3 divisions from SLAM-HSCs.
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data.

claim: At 24 hr, most families were composed of only one cell type.
source: At 24 hr, most families were composed of only one cell type (Figure 4A), but at 48 hr more families produced several cell types (Figure 4B), indicating that downstream asymmetries in the fate occur after a largely symmetric first division (Figure 2G).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: At 48 hr more families produced several cell types, indicating that downstream asymmetries in the fate occur after a largely symmetric first division.
source: At 24 hr, most families were composed of only one cell type (Figure 4A), but at 48 hr more families produced several cell types (Figure 4B), indicating that downstream asymmetries in the fate occur after a largely symmetric first division (Figure 2G).
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4B, and the indication is an inference from the data.

claim: Permutation tests on phenotypically defined cell types revealed that families exhibited significantly more similarity than would be expected if there was no family component, both at 24 hr and at 48 hr.
source: Permutation tests on phenotypically defined cell types revealed that families exhibited significantly more similarity than would be expected if there was no family component, both at 24 hr (Figure 4A) and at 48 hr (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: Within-family similarity in fate is visible by the co-localization of cells from the same family on the UMAP.
source: This within-family similarity in fate is visible by the co-localization of cells from the same family on the UMAP (Figure 4C).
evidence: The observation is based on UMAP visualization of experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SLAM-HSC, ST-HSC, and MPP families are highly concordant in division and share similar differentiation outcomes in vitro, while population-level diversity in proliferation and cell types arises from heterogeneity across families.
source: Thus, SLAM-HSC, ST-HSC, and MPP families are highly concordant in division and share similar differentiation outcomes in vitro, while population-level diversity in proliferation and cell types arises from heterogeneity across families.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: Comparison of the median fluorescent intensities of markers from ancestors during sort with those obtained from daughters at each of the two time points revealed clear correlation between the two.
source: Comparison of the median fluorescent intensities of markers from ancestors during sort with those obtained from daughters at each of the two time points (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) revealed clear correlation between the two, supporting the hypothesis that ancestor surface expression markers were instructive in the within-family homogeneity in division progression and differentiation.
evidence: The observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Ancestor surface expression markers were instructive in the within-family homogeneity in division progression and differentiation.
source: Comparison of the median fluorescent intensities of markers from ancestors during sort with those obtained from daughters at each of the two time points (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) revealed clear correlation between the two, supporting the hypothesis that ancestor surface expression markers were instructive in the within-family homogeneity in division progression and differentiation.
evidence: The hypothesis is supported by the correlation observed in experimental data.

claim: Across both cocktails and time points, only cell surface markers on ancestral SLAM-HSCs were consistently instructive for division progression.
source: Across both cocktails and time points, only cell surface markers on ancestral SLAM-HSCs were consistently instructive for division progression.
evidence: The observation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: CD48 correlated positively with division progression in SLAM-HSCs, with its strongest effect at 24 hr.
source: CD48 correlated positively, with its strongest effect at 24 hr, and Sca-1 correlated negatively, while at 48 hr c-Kit correlated positively (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Sca-1 correlated negatively with division progression in SLAM-HSCs.
source: CD48 correlated positively, with its strongest effect at 24 hr, and Sca-1 correlated negatively, while at 48 hr c-Kit correlated positively (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: At 48 hr c-Kit correlated positively with division progression in SLAM-HSCs.
source: CD48 correlated positively, with its strongest effect at 24 hr, and Sca-1 correlated negatively, while at 48 hr c-Kit correlated positively (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: For both ST-HSCs and MPPs, none of the phenotypic markers exhibited strong correlation with division progression, indicating the need to identify other markers.
source: Notably, for both ST-HSCs and MPPs, even though the family data clearly indicate that there is a familial component to division progression (Figure 2H), none of the phenotypic markers exhibited strong correlation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), indicating the need to identify other markers.
evidence: The observation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, and the indication is an inference from the data.

claim: For SLAM-HSCs, at 24 and 48 hr in both cocktails, Sca-1 expression provided a strong positive correlation to self-renewal and a negative one to production of PreMegE.
source: For SLAM-HSCs, at 24 and 48 hr in both cocktails, Sca-1 expression provided a strong positive correlation to self-renewal and a negative one to production of PreMegE.
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: At 48 hr, c-Kit presented the inverse dependency to Sca-1 in SLAM-HSCs.
source: At 48 hr, c-Kit presented the inverse dependency to Sca-1.
evidence: The observation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: At 24 and 48 hr, CD48 correlated negatively to self-renewal and positively to production of PreMegE when IL-3 and IL-6 are added in SLAM-HSCs.
source: At 24 and 48 hr, CD48 correlated negatively to self-renewal and positively to production of PreMegE when IL-3 and IL-6 are added.
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: c-Kit and Sca-1 expression levels of SLAM-HSCs act as intrinsic markers for both familial progression and differentiation with high Sca-1 expression and low c-Kit expression leading to less division (Wilson et al., 2015; Grinenko et al., 2014; Morcos et al., 2017) and less differentiation (Shin et al., 2014), and potentially resulting in better engraftment (Wilson et al., 2015; Grinenko et al., 2014; Shin et al., 2014).
source: As cocktail composition did not have a major impact on the relationship between familial fate and ancestral expression, these results were suggestive that c-Kit and Sca-1 expression levels of SLAM-HSCs act as intrinsic markers for both familial progression and differentiation with high Sca-1 expression and low c-Kit expression leading to less division (Wilson et al., 2015; Grinenko et al., 2014; Morcos et al., 2017) and less differentiation (Shin et al., 2014), and potentially resulting in better engraftment (Wilson et al., 2015; Grinenko et al., 2014; Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: The suggestion is based on experimental data and is consistent with multiple previous studies.

claim: Low ancestral CD48 expression level has been reported to result in less division (Pietras et al., 2015; Akinduro et al., 2018), but the data indicates its relationship to differentiation is dependent on extrinsic signals.
source: While low ancestral CD48 expression level has been reported to result in less division (Pietras et al., 2015; Akinduro et al., 2018), our data indicates its relationship to differentiation is dependent on extrinsic signals.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data and contrasts with previous literature regarding the relationship to differentiation.

claim: For ST-HSCs, the ancestral level of CD48 and Sca-1 consistently correlated negatively and positively, respectively, with de-differentiation to SLAM-HSC in the cocktail with IL-3 and IL-6 at both time points.
source: For ST-HSCs, the ancestral level of CD48 and Sca-1 consistently correlated negatively and positively, respectively, with de-differentiation to SLAM-HSC in the cocktail with IL-3 and IL-6 at both time points (Figures 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figures 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Differentiation to GMP from ST-HSC, which occurred only in 48 hr data, correlated positively and negatively with the ancestral level of CD48 and Sca-1, respectively (Morcos et al., 2017).
source: Differentiation to GMP, which occurred only in 48 hr data, correlated positively and negatively with the ancestral level of CD48 and Sca-1, respectively (Figure 4E; Morcos et al., 2017).
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4E and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Differentiation to GMP from ST-HSC was dependent on the parental level of CD48 and Sca-1, whereas the de-differentiation to SLAM-HSC is dependent on both extrinsic factors (IL-3 and IL-6) and the intrinsic ancestral level of CD48 and Sca-1.
source: Therefore, differentiation to GMP from ST-HSC was dependent on the parental level of CD48 and Sca-1, whereas the de-differentiation to SLAM-HSC is dependent on both extrinsic factors (IL-3 and IL-6) and the intrinsic ancestral level of CD48 and Sca-1.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: The differentiation from MPPs to GMPs that was observed to occur by 48 hr correlated negatively with Sca-1 ancestral expression (Morcos et al., 2017) in both cocktails.
source: The differentiation from MPPs to GMPs that was observed to occur by 48 hr correlated negatively with Sca-1 ancestral expression (Morcos et al., 2017) in both cocktails.
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Differentiation from MPPs to GMPs also negatively correlated with Flt3 ancestral expression, but only in the cocktail without IL-3 and IL-6.
source: It also negatively correlated with Flt3 ancestral expression, but only in the cocktail without IL-3 and IL-6 (Figure 4E).
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: In the presence of IL-3 and IL-6, differentiation from MPP to GMP positively correlated with c-Kit ancestral expression.
source: In the presence of IL-3 and IL-6, instead, differentiation from MPP to GMP positively correlated with c-Kit ancestral expression.
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Differentiation from MPP to CMP/MEP occurred only at 48 hr in the cocktail without IL-3 and IL-6, and then correlated positively with c-Kit.
source: Differentiation from MPP to CMP/MEP occurred only at 48 hr in the cocktail without IL-3 and IL-6, and then correlated positively with c-Kit (Figure 4E).
evidence: The correlation is based on statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Differentiation to GMP from MPP is dependent on the intrinsic ancestral level of Sca-1, whereas the differentiation to CMP/MEP is dependent on both extrinsic factors (IL-3 and IL-6) and the intrinsic ancestral level of c-Kit.
source: Thus, differentiation to GMP from MPP is dependent on the intrinsic ancestral level of Sca-1, whereas the differentiation to CMP/MEP is dependent on both extrinsic factors (IL-3 and IL-6) and the intrinsic ancestral level of c-Kit.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: The concordance in division and similarity in fate within families is partially explained by the surface expression marker used to phenotype ancestors, but both intrinsic and extrinsic factors act to direct familial fate.
source: Overall, the concordance in division and similarity in fate within families is partially explained by the surface expression marker used to phenotype ancestors, but both intrinsic and extrinsic factors act to direct familial fate.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: Despite substantial population-level heterogeneity, offspring cells derived from a single ancestor are highly concordant in their division progression and exhibit familial effects on differentiation.
source: Its use with HSPCs revealed that despite substantial population-level heterogeneity amongst offspring cells derived from a single ancestor are highly concordant in their division progression and exhibit familial effects on differentiation.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: The restriction in differentiated cell types within each family is propagated primarily through symmetric first divisions.
source: The restriction in differentiated cell types within each family is propagated primarily through symmetric first divisions.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: Although each family is composed of several cell types, the overall collection of cell types observed in a population is composed of homogeneous families from heterogeneous ancestors.
source: Although each family is composed of several cell types, the overall collection of cell types observed in a population is composed of homogeneous families from heterogeneous ancestors.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data.

claim: The generation of a diversity of cell types is presently assumed to result from a diversification within every family.
source: The generation of a diversity of cell types is presently assumed to result from a diversification within every family, and methods for inferring differentiation trajectories using single-cell RNA sequencing data from snapshot data assume that cells all behave independently (Trapnell et al., 2014; Bendall et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim describes a current assumption in the field and cites relevant literature.

claim: Methods for inferring differentiation trajectories using single-cell RNA sequencing data from snapshot data assume that cells all behave independently (Trapnell et al., 2014; Bendall et al., 2014).
source: The generation of a diversity of cell types is presently assumed to result from a diversification within every family, and methods for inferring differentiation trajectories using single-cell RNA sequencing data from snapshot data assume that cells all behave independently (Trapnell et al., 2014; Bendall et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim describes a current assumption in computational methods and cites relevant literature.

claim: The findings establish that familial dependencies that are currently unmeasured exist within the population and call for a revision of the assumption of independent fate decision by cells along the hematopoietic tree.
source: Consistent with previous observations of early lineage priming (Müller-Sieburg et al., 2002; Perié and Duffy, 2016; Paul et al., 2016; Hoppe et al., 2016), our findings establish that familial dependencies that are currently unmeasured exist within the population and call for a revision of the assumption of independent fate decision by cells along the hematopoietic tree.
evidence: The conclusion is based on analysis of experimental data and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Ancestral cell surface expression of markers used for phenotyping serves as correlates that partially predict some of these familial properties.
source: Ancestral cell surface expression of markers used for phenotyping serves as correlates that partially predict some of these familial properties, but, in particular, a correlate that explains the highly heritable division progression of ST-HSC and MPP families is not contained within them.

claim: HSCs can sequentially reconstitute the blood system of several hosts (Ross et al., 1982).
source: It is well-established that HSCs can sequentially reconstitute the blood system of several hosts (Ross et al., 1982), leading to the inference that HSCs must be able to maintain themselves (Morrison and Kimble, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Only a few HSCs reconstitute all of the blood lineages, with the rest being either restricted in the number of lineages they produce (Yamamoto et al., 2013; Sanjuan-Pla et al., 2013; Rodriguez-Fraticelli et al., 2018; Carrelha et al., 2018) or having a bias or imbalance in the proportion of cell types they create (Dykstra et al., 2007; Müller-Sieburg et al., 2004).
source: Recent single-cell transplantation and cellular barcoding experiments have revealed that only a few HSCs reconstitute all of the blood lineages, with the rest being either restricted in the number of lineages they produce (Yamamoto et al., 2013; Sanjuan-Pla et al., 2013; Rodriguez-Fraticelli et al., 2018; Carrelha et al., 2018) or having a bias or imbalance in the proportion of cell types they create (Dykstra et al., 2007; Müller-Sieburg et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Some HSCs produce only megakaryocytes (Rodriguez-Fraticelli et al., 2018; Carrelha et al., 2018).
source: As examples of lineage restriction, it has been reported that some HSCs produce only megakaryocytes (Rodriguez-Fraticelli et al., 2018; Carrelha et al., 2018), while others produce only myeloid cells, megakaryocytes, and erythrocytes (Yamamoto et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BM cells were obtained from wild-type C57BL/6 mice of 8–16 weeks of age.

evidence: The experimental procedure is described in the methods.

claim: BM cells were MACS enriched for c-Kit+ cells using CD117 MicroBeads Ultrapure.
source: BM cells were MACS enriched for c-Kit+ cells using CD117 MicroBeads Ultrapure (Miltenyi Biotec cat #130-091-224) according to the manufacturer's protocol.
evidence: The experimental procedure is described in the methods.

claim: Cells were cultured at 37°C under 5% CO2 in 100 µl of StemSpan serum-free expansion medium supplemented with cytokines.
source: Cells were cultured at 37°C under 5% CO2 in 100 µl of StemSpan serum-free expansion medium (Stemcell Technologies 9650) supplemented with 50 ng/ml murine recombinant thrombopoietin (TPO, Sigma-Aldrich SRP3236-10UG) and 100 ng/ml stem cell factor (SCF) or 50 ng/ml TPO, 100 ng/ml SCF, 20 ng/ml IL-3, and 100 ng/ml IL-6 (Ema et al., 2000; Roch et al., 2017).
evidence: The experimental procedure is described in the methods.

claim: The recovery estimate per well was circa 70% based on beads-based estimate.
source: Cells from each well were analyzed at 4°C using a ZE5 Flow cytometer (BioRad) with a recovery estimate of circa 70% per well (beads-based estimate, data not shown).
evidence: The recovery rate is stated based on experimental measurements.
